//: One program for the whole monorepo, not project references.
References require `composite`, and therefore real `.d.ts` emit. While packages are
consumed from source, one program checks exactly the same thing in a single pass.
Once packages are consumed from build output this becomes project references,
and `paths` leaves tsconfig.base.json at the same time.
Each package keeps its own tsconfig.json for `pnpm --filter ... typecheck` and for the
editor: it shows WHAT the package sees when looked at alone.
The one thing a single program cannot hold is a second JSX dialect. `jsx` and
`jsxImportSource` are per-PROGRAM, and Solid compiles JSX into its own reactive calls
with its own `JSX` namespace — so a Solid `.tsx` checked under React's setting types
every element as `React.JSX.Element` and every Solid component rejects it. That package
is excluded here and checked by its own config, which `pnpm run check:bindings` runs.
An exclusion nobody runs is an exclusion nobody notices, which is why it has a script.
